title: Minimax Estimation of Shift Policy Values for Functional Treatments under Singular Laws
banked_reason: D0.5.G graded incremental below field: paper_score_ceiling 6.2 < ceiling_for_field 7.4; constructive_object_missing@oeq:critical-scalar-modulus, salvageable=false.
gap_reasons: At b=a+1/2 it does not deliver the advertised explicit one-dimensional constant-factor modulus, logarithmic correction, or scalar-selected attaining weight; R_n is instead compared with an abstract infinite-dimensional modulus, so references to a completed three-regime frontier overstate what is resolved at equality.

More seriously, in the singular regime the assumptions identify the continuous observed-regression extension but do not imply that this extension equals x↦E[Y^x] on Q_h-relevant P_A-null sets, so the proved target is not an identified causal policy value even though the framing invokes causal effects and guidance for functional-policy analysts.

The promised equality-boundary constant-factor one-dimensional modulus and scalar-selected observable attaining weight remain open; the abstract omega_n and an existential approximate affine minimizer do not deliver the stated critical tuning rule or usable interval construction.
proof_attempt_summary: Discovery proved matched logarithmic risk and honest-length rates on the singular side, a regular root-n result, and a polynomial exponent at the equality boundary. It reduced the critical risk to an abstract optimal-recovery modulus, but the one-scale clipped weight is polynomially suboptimal and no multiscale constant-factor scalar modulus or matching explicit weight was derived. The D0.5 panel also found an off-support causal interpretation gap and graded the delivered package incremental below the field floor; the independent validity gate confirmed a downgraded terminal outcome.
tldr: A deterministic translated-Gaussian observed-law value is point identified through the unique continuous regression version even when the observational and policy treatment laws are mutually singular. For a known Gaussian treatment law and bounded global Lipschitz Bernoulli regression, the paper gives matching logarithmic minimax risk and honest interval length below the Cameron--Martin boundary, the exact magnitude-dependent polynomial log-slope and exact-modulus honest length at the boundary, and the known-law efficiency bound with an attaining one-step interval above the boundary. A constant-factor one-dimensional evaluation of the critical modulus, including its logarithmic correction and an explicit scalar-selected attaining weight, remains open.
gap: Functional-policy papers give identification and regular estimator theory under finite-score tail and density-ratio conditions, while general off-policy work gives abstract moduli and reproducing-kernel Hilbert-space attainment. No located source evaluates the bounded-Lipschitz deterministic translated-Gaussian policy value at or below mutual singularity.
fill: The project combines legal Bernoulli causal lower experiments, finite-coordinate and affine optimal-recovery estimators, and bias-aware intervals into a three-regime phase diagram. Its distinctive contribution is the constant-factor scalar modulus and observable attaining weight at \(b=a+1/2\).
